properties.decision:
UNDECIDED. Raised by Anthony 2026-07-25 from his own situation: he is in Long Island, his brother is in Washington State, they want to work on one design at the same time and to see each other's projects. FOUR ROADS, and the middle ones are not the obvious winners. (a) GIT IS ALREADY THE CENTRAL SERVER — the design is a file in the repo, the repo already spans both coasts, and the claims layer that shipped 2026-07-25 already answers "who has what in hand" the moment either side pulls. Nothing to host, nothing to secure, nothing to pay for, and no new place for the design to live. What it cannot do is tell you about a claim before the other person pushes. (b) A HOSTED MCP over HTTPS — one server process holding the graph, both people's agents connecting to it, so a claim is visible the moment it is made and a design is reachable by someone who never cloned the repo. Costs: ~~reflow2-mcp serves stdio only today (rmcp's streamable-HTTP transport exists, the binary does not use it)~~ **— THAT CLAIM IS STALE, see the 2026-08-26 correction below —** authentication does not exist at all, and it puts the design on a machine — which weakens but does not erase dec:repo-file-embedded's objection, since the machine would be Anthony's own droplet rather than a vendor's. NOTE WHAT MAKES (b) CHEAPER THAN IT LOOKS: one server process with many clients is ALREADY compatible with the single-writer store, because there is still exactly one writer — the server. (c) HYBRID — host a read/publish surface for reaching and browsing designs, keep writes local and merge through git, so the durable record never moves. THE CHEAPEST FIRST CUT, worth naming because it needs almost no core work: one server process PER PROJECT, each with its own graph path and its own token, and project selection becomes which URL the agent points at — no graph_id plumbing, no multi-tenancy, and a per-project blast radius if one goes wrong. A private tailnet instead of public TLS removes the authentication problem for exactly two people, which is the population this actually has. (d) ONE LIVE SHARED WORKING TREE on a droplet — both people editing the same checkout simultaneously, seeing each other's edits, with a push to a "true" git repo every so often for permanent storage (Anthony, 2026-07-25). THE DESIGN HALF OF THIS IS (b) AND IS SOUND; THE CODE HALF INVERTS THE PROPERTY IT IS REACHING FOR. A shared checkout does not remove conflicts, it removes conflict DETECTION: with one copy there is no common ancestor to merge against, so two agents doing read-modify-write on one file interleave into last-write-wins with no marker, no three-way merge and nothing to review — strictly less safe than what they have now. It also shares the things git assumes are private (one index, one HEAD, one branch: `git checkout` on his side changes files under her mid-edit), shares the build directory and the graph's single-writer lock, and makes the droplet a single point of failure for two people who can currently both work on a plane. The batched push is its own cost: history granularity, attribution and bisect all collapse into one commit, the gates that are supposed to gate a commit are replaced by a timer, and "every so often" is precisely the size of the loss window when the droplet dies.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SHARPENED 2026-08-11 — THE PUBLISHING CASE ARRIVES WITH A NAME, AND IT BREAKS AN ASSUMPTION EVERY OPTION ABOVE SHARES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony is thinking out loud; nothing here settles this decision, which stays `proposed`.

⭐ DELIBERATELY SHARPENED RATHER THAN OPENED AS A NEW NODE. This node's own rationale already named the gap it is being filled with — "what it does NOT deliver is the publishing case, and that is the strongest argument on the hosted side" — so a second node would have been the near-duplicate the search-first rule exists to prevent. What follows is new EVIDENCE on the same question, not a new question.

HIS WORDS, 2026-08-11: "I want to use reflow2 within flo2. it is purposefully designed to allow collaboration on projects via a web app. if one user posts some brainstorm idea or identifies gaps, the other user shouldn't have to run some terminal commands in order to see that (especially non technical people using web app where no CLI exists)."

⭐⭐ THE ASSUMPTION THAT JUST BROKE, and it is the reason this is worth re-weighing rather than merely noting. EVERY option above was weighed for TWO TECHNICAL PEOPLE WITH TERMINALS. Option (a) — "git is already the central server" — is only free if both parties can run git. The moment one participant is a non-technical user of a web app, (a) stops being free and starts being impossible: there is no shell to run `git pull` in, no checkout to pull into, and no way to run the import that makes a pulled file readable by the tools.

THE CONCRETE FRICTION HE IS OBJECTING TO, measured today rather than supposed: for a second person to SEE a brainstormed idea in a form the tools can answer questions about, they must today (1) `git pull`, (2) run `reflow2-mcp --graph-path .reflow2/graph --import docs/design/reflow2.json`, and (3) have a merge driver configured per-clone or meet a raw text conflict in a 4 MB JSON file. That is three technical steps between one person recording a thought and another person seeing it. For an agent-driven CLI user it is friction; for a web-app user it is a wall.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE, stated separately so neither is overclaimed:
- It does NOT re-open `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (accepted 2026-07-25, "no hosted service"). That decision answered how two WRITERS avoid clobbering each other, and its rejection of hosting rested on `req:persistence` and `req:invocation` — both of which describe where a design DURABLY LIVES. A read/publish surface does not move the durable record, which is exactly why option (c) exists here.
- It DOES weaken option (a) as a general answer, because (a)'s cheapness was priced for participants who all have a shell.
- ⚠️ It sits against `dec:one-process-many-stores` (ACCEPTED, conditional) and `rule:per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global`, which already contemplate a hosted reflow2 holding N single-writer stores. So the hosted direction is NOT unexplored ground — it is partly built toward, and `req:a-session-cannot-address-another-design` is the guard that must be proven before it ships.
- `fact:the-hosted-case-breaks-the-git-transport-and-the-access-topology-is-now-stated` already recorded the same collision from the other side, on 2026-08-09.

THE NEW QUESTION THIS RAISES, which none of (a)–(d) answers: WHO IS THE WRITER when the participant is a web-app user? reflow2's loop is ask-the-human-and-record-an-ATTRIBUTABLE-answer. Today attribution comes from a Contributor a local agent names. Through a web app, the app is the MCP client and the human is behind it — so either flo2 passes identity through to reflow2 on every write, or every contribution from that surface is attributed to "flo2" and the confirmation ledger stops meaning what it says. ⭐ THAT IS A HARDER PROBLEM THAN THE TRANSPORT, and it is the one most likely to be discovered late.

⚠️ A REPO-BOUNDARY NOTE, so nobody skips it: flo2 is a SEPARATE PROJECT with its own design graph and its own owners. Nothing here may be built into flo2 from this repo without Anthony's word (AGENTS.md rule 6). What reflow2 can decide alone is whether it OFFERS a surface flo2 could consume; whether flo2 consumes it is flo2's decision to record.

NOT DECIDED, and deliberately not ranked. Option (c) — publish/read hosted, writes stay local — is the one this evidence pushes hardest on, but it is also the one whose attribution story is least worked out.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ SHARPENED 2026-08-26 — THE TRANSPORT COST IN OPTION (b) WAS ALREADY PAID, AND THIS NODE HAS BEEN CARRYING A STALE CLAIM FOR A MONTH
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING. Sharpened rather than forked, following this node's own 2026-08-11 precedent: new evidence on the same question.

Anthony brought research: *"STDIO Transport (One-to-One): the MCP server runs as a local child process spawned directly by a single client... a strict, private 1:1 pipe... It cannot be shared with other clients. HTTP / SSE Transport (Many-to-One): the MCP server operates as an independent, centralized service running on a port. This allows multiple distinct clients over the network to connect, authenticate, and send concurrent requests to the same server process."*

🛑 **THAT RESEARCH IS CORRECT AND IT FALSIFIES A COST LINE IN OPTION (b) ABOVE.** This node says reflow2-mcp *"serves stdio only today (rmcp's streamable-HTTP transport exists, the binary does not use it)"*. **That was true on 2026-07-25 and became false in v0.14.0.** Verified on the binary 2026-08-26:

    --http <ADDR>   "Serve over HTTP on this address instead of stdio, so SEVERAL sessions
                     share one design (req:sessions-share-a-graph). One process holds the
                     graph — the store is single-writer, and with one server there is still
                     exactly one writer — while every client session gets its own seat."

`cap:shared-sessions` is BUILT and `ver:shared-sessions` — *"Two sessions share one design over real HTTP, with seats that differ"* — is PASSING. `cmp:mcp-http`, `cmp:shared` and `cmp:proxy` are the three components that do it. A shared server was running on `http://127.0.0.1:40233/` during this very session.

⭐ **SO OPTION (b)'s REMAINING COST IS AUTHENTICATION AND REACHABILITY, NOT TRANSPORT.** The flag's own help says it: *"Bind to a loopback or tailnet address: there is no authentication yet, so anything that can reach the port can write the design."* The many-to-one server Anthony's research describes is not a thing reflow2 would have to build — it is a thing reflow2 already runs, on loopback, every day.

⭐ **AND IT INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMS OPTION (c)'s CHEAPEST-FIRST-CUT.** That option already proposed *"one server process PER PROJECT, each with its own graph path and its own token"* and *"a private tailnet instead of public TLS"*. The binary's own help text now recommends exactly that binding. The gap between (c)-as-written and (c)-as-shipped is a token and a non-loopback bind.

📌 **A CONSEQUENCE FOR `rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground`, settled the same day.** If reflow2 targets ANY MCP CLIENT, and several DIFFERENT products are to work one design at once — Claude Code and Cursor on the same graph — then stdio cannot serve them, because stdio is 1:1 with the process that spawned it. **Multi-product collaboration is an HTTP-only capability by protocol construction, not by implementation choice.** That is a stronger argument for the hosted direction than any of (a)–(d) made, and none of them made it.

⚠️ WHAT IS STILL UNCHANGED AND MUST NOT BE READ AS SOLVED: the attribution question from 2026-08-11 — who is the writer when the client is a web app — is untouched by any of this. Transport was never the hard half.
properties.name: DECIDED — option (c): a hosted READ/PUBLISH surface, writes stay local, one server per project on a tailnet
properties.rationale:
Settled by Anthony 2026-08-26, after a month open, choosing option (c) from four roads put to him with corrected costs.

WHY THE COSTS WERE RE-PUT RATHER THAN THE OLD ONES REUSED: this node had carried a stale claim since 2026-07-25 — that reflow2-mcp "serves stdio only" — which became false in v0.14.0. Deciding on the old text would have meant deciding against a cost estimate that was wrong in the direction that mattered, since the transport both (b) and (c) need is BUILT and passing. The correction and its verification are written into the decision text above.

WHAT MAKES (c) THE RIGHT SHAPE RATHER THAN MERELY THE CHEAP ONE: the durable record does not move. `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (accepted 2026-07-25, no hosted service) rested on `req:persistence` and `req:invocation`, both of which describe where a design DURABLY LIVES — and a read/publish surface leaves that in the repo. So this is not a reversal of that decision; it is the option that was always compatible with it, which is why (c) existed among the original four.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, KEPT BECAUSE CHOOSING DOES NOT ANSWER IT: (c) is the road whose ATTRIBUTION story is least worked out. Who is the writer when the participant is a web-app user? Today attribution comes from a Contributor a local agent names; through flo2 the app is the MCP client and the human is behind it. Nothing in this choice answers that, and the node has flagged it as harder than the transport since 2026-08-11. **It is now the blocking question rather than a footnote.**

ALSO UNCHANGED: a hosted surface adds a second place a design is reachable from, which is a real change to the threat surface even on a tailnet, and authentication does not exist at all today. The binary's own `--http` help says so — "there is no authentication yet, so anything that can reach the port can write the design."

WHAT IS NOT YET DECIDED AND MUST NOT BE READ INTO THIS: whether flo2 consumes the surface. flo2 is a separate project with its own graph and owners (AGENTS.md rule 6). This settles only that reflow2 OFFERS one.
